(CNN) -- Police are searching for any other alleged victims of a Sunday school teacher accused of raping and killing an 8-year-old girl from Tracy, California. Melissa Huckaby is charged with killing 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, who was a friend of her own daughter. "We are asking the public if they have any indication that any of their children may have had inappropriate contact with [the suspect] to contact us," Tracy Police Sgt. Tony Sheneman said Tuesday evening. "There has been no indication that this has happened. But she is a Sunday school teacher and did have contact with children, so that is why we are asking." Melissa Huckaby, 28, was arrested and charged with killing and raping 8-year-old Sandra Cantu, a friend of her 5-year-old daughter. Huckaby, wearing red jail scrubs over a white T-shirt, was in court Tuesday for an arraignment. She was charged with murder, kidnapping, the performance of a lewd and lascivious act on a child under 14 and rape by instrument. If convicted, Huckaby would face the death penalty or life in prison without parole, San Joaquin County District Attorney James Willett told reporters after the hearing. A decision on whether to seek the death penalty will be made later, he said. Huckaby did not enter a plea or speak during the court hearing, although she flinched when Sandra Cantu's name was spoken, and she cried at times. Sandra's body was found April 6, stuffed into a suitcase and submerged in a pond at a dairy farm. Huckaby was arrested Friday night after questioning by police. Sandra was last seen alive March 27 in the mobile home park where she lived with her family -- the same mobile home park where Huckaby lives with her daughter. The two children were close friends and played together frequently, police said. Huckaby is the granddaughter of Clifford Lane Lawless, pastor of Clover Road Baptist Church near the mobile home park, and she taught Sunday school at the church, police have said. The church was searched as part of the investigation into Sandra's disappearance and death. Before her arrest, Huckaby acknowledged to a newspaper reporter that she owned the suitcase that contained Sandra's body. But Huckaby said the suitcase had been stolen. Willett declined to comment on any of the evidence or allegations in the case, saying evidence would be presented in court. A memorial ceremony is scheduled for Sandra at 1 p.m. Thursday at a high school in Tracy, police said. -- CNN's Ninette Sosa contributed to this report.

**A Betrayal of Trust: The Tragic Murder of Sandra Cantu and the Arrest of Melissa Huckaby**

TRACY, Calif. — In the spring of 2009, the quiet, close-knit agricultural community of Tracy, California, was shattered by a tragedy that quickly gripped the nation. What began as a desperate search for a missing eight-year-old girl ended in a horrific discovery, leading to the arrest of an unlikely suspect—a local Sunday school teacher who lived just doors away from the victim.

### The Disappearance and the Search

On March 27, 2009, eight-year-old Sandra Cantu vanished from the Orchard Acres Mobile Home Park. Surveillance video captured the cheerful young girl playfully skipping past the park’s visitor center, wearing a pink shirt and leggings, on her way to play at a neighbor's house. She never returned home. 

For ten agonizing days, the community rallied behind the Cantu family. Hundreds of volunteers, alongside local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, scoured the surrounding fields, canal systems, and residential neighborhoods. Ribbons in Sandra's favorite color, pink, were tied to trees and light posts throughout Tracy as residents held candlelight vigils, praying for her safe return.

### A Horrific Discovery

The desperate search came to a devastating end on April 6, 2009. Farmworkers draining an agricultural irrigation pond—located roughly two miles from the mobile home park—noticed a dark object submerged in the shallow water. Upon further inspection, authorities recovered a heavy black Eddie Bauer suitcase. 

Inside the luggage was the body of young Sandra Cantu. 

Autopsy results confirmed the town's worst fears: Sandra had been sexually assaulted, murdered, and stuffed into the suitcase before being disposed of in the pond. The gruesome nature of the crime sent shockwaves through San Joaquin County and escalated the investigation into a high-priority homicide case.

### The Unlikely Suspect

Suspicion quickly fell upon 28-year-old Melissa Huckaby. Huckaby was not a stranger to Sandra; she lived in the same mobile home park, her own daughter was a frequent playmate of Sandra’s, and her grandfather was a pastor at a local church where Huckaby taught Sunday school. 

In the days leading up to the discovery of the body, Huckaby had inserted herself into the media narrative. She offered bizarre and conflicting statements to local reporters, even claiming that the suitcase used to hide Sandra's body had been stolen from her driveway on the day Sandra disappeared. 

However, investigators uncovered critical physical evidence and inconsistencies in Huckaby’s timeline. Search warrants executed at her home and the local church revealed evidence linking her directly to the crime, including tire tracks at the pond matching her vehicle and materials inside the church basement that tied her to the victim.

### Formal Charges and a Broader Appeal

On April 10, 2009, following hours of intensive police interrogation, Melissa Huckaby was formally arrested. Prosecutors swiftly filed charges against her, including first-degree murder with special circumstances for kidnapping, rape by instrument, and lewd acts upon a child. 

The arrest of a Sunday school teacher—someone in a position of authority and moral trust—stunned the public. Given Huckaby’s role as a religious instructor, caregiver, and volunteer, police in Tracy took the unusual step of launching a broader appeal to the public. Authorities urged parents and community members across northern California to come forward with any information regarding Huckaby’s past behavior, seeking to determine if there were other unrecorded child victims.

### Facing Ultimate Justice

With the special circumstance allegations attached to the charges, San Joaquin County prosecutors indicated that Huckaby would face the most severe penalties available under California law: life imprisonment without the possibility of parole, or the death penalty. 

The case left an indelible scar on the city of Tracy. For the family of Sandra Cantu, the arrest provided answers, but no true comfort for the sudden and brutal loss of a bright, vibrant child whose trust was so cruelly abused by a neighbor she considered a friend.

Jennings is currently being held without bail at the San Joaquin County Jail. Her initial court arraignment is scheduled for Monday morning at the San Joaquin County Superior Court.

The District Attorney’s Office stated that prosecutors are evaluating whether to seek special circumstances charges, which could make the case eligible for the death penalty or life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. 

It was not immediately clear if Jennings has retained legal counsel.

Outside the Oakridge Mobile Home Park, a makeshift memorial of stuffed animals, pink balloons, and lit candles continued to grow on Saturday as neighbors gathered to mourn.

"Maya was a bright, smiling light in this park," her uncle, Ramon Gomez, said in a brief statement on behalf of the family. "We are heartbroken, but we demand justice for our little girl."
